w: The Indian Ambassador for South Africa, H.E. Niranjan Desai, came for Swamishri's darshan. In his address he described Swamishri as the global ambassador of Hindu tradition and culture.

Volunteers' Day During the evening assembly, a drama "Offering Everything" was performed by the volunteers. The drama showed the services of volunteers in the face of insult, adverse weather and hunger. Finally Swamishri, in his blessings, highlighted the sacrifice and service of the volunteers.

Prior to Swamishri's morning puja devotees had gathered for the Rath Yatra celebration in the mandir precincts, Amdavad. When Swamishri arrived the utsav murti of Maharaj was arranged in a decorated small chariot and Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was placed in a small rath that was a replica of the chariot in Jagannathpuri. Children were colorfully dressed with dance sticks in their hands. Swamishri, after darshan and arti of Thakorji in the mandir, performed pujan of the utsav murti and Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and pulled the rope of the chariot and circumambulated the mandir. After performing five pradakshinas the Rath Yatra festival concluded and Swamishri performed his morning puja.

In the evening assembly, a rath y atra of Thakorji was carried out in the assembly hall. Swamishri then operated the remote control console and steered the rath of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj on stage. Thereafter a drama on Brahmanand Swami's life was brilliantly performed by the youths of Amdavad Yuvak Mandal.
Yuvak - Yuvati National Convention Yuvaks and yuvatis arrived from all over North America to take part in the National Convention at the Orange County Convention Center in Orlando, Florida.

In the welcome assembly, yuvaks heartily welcomed Shri Harikrishna Maharaj on a palanquin and Swamishri on a chariot, dancing all around them. The theme of the convention, ‘Vicharan’, was explained by senior sadhus, who recounted incidents from over the years of the physical and mental hardships Swamishri has endured on his divine travels.

As part of the Children’s Day celebration the evening assembly had various presentations by children. Then Swamishri blessed the assembly, “In the past talks from the Ramayan, Bhagvat, etc. Nowadays when they are asked, children question, Who is Ram? Who is Krishna? They do not know about God or who has given this body. So, how can virtues be developed? Merely planting a tree is not enough, but it has to be provided water and fertilizer. Only then will it grow and give fruits. Just as trees are nurtured in this way, children, too, must be nurtured85 Dhruv and Prahlad were taught good values from childhood by their mothers85 Happiness in life is due to our dharma and virtues85 Peace and happiness is obtained from God.”
Friday, 1 July 2005 (Jeth vad 10, Samvat 2061), Jamnagar
Pramukh Swami Maharaj's reading of letters was almost over. Swamishri called into the room every youth who had come from abroad, and those from India too, to benefit from his company.

The youths who had come from abroad naturally did not find village life easy. On top of that, in Bhadra they had become very fed up because of the plague of flies. Catching this nerve of theirs, Swamishri said, "How was it in Bhadra?"
"It did not suit us much," the youths admitted frankly.

Hearing this, Swamishri said, "Bhadra is the birthplace of Gunatitanand Swami; it is sanctified by great prasadi. It is a village, so the rain makes it muddy, but now you know what villages in India are like, don't you? When you go back, do not say that everything was dirty. Just as the people here have got used to it, you too should get used to it. Wherever you are, you should adjust to whatever facilities you get. So when you go back, do not say it is dirty."
"It may be dirty on the outside, but inside India is very good," Sheel replied.

"Just so! Take that virtue. The religious feeling and family feeling that there are in India you will not find abroad. There, you do not even know what is going on next door, and here, if you go to someone's home, see how people welcome you! Here, if you are a guest, even if the house is small they will give you a place to stay in their home, and there they put you in a hotel. That is how our culture is. The joy is in living together as a community, and there no one lives together with each other. So there is nothing like India."

Swamishri celebrated the Mandir patotsav (anniversary) on 1 July and devotees celebrated Guru Bhakti Din (3 July). In the evening celebration assembly of BAPS Centenary Year Swamishri was festively welcomed by the Dallas band and flag-waving devotees. Prior to Swamishri’s arrival speeches by Viveksagar Swami and Ishwarcharan Swami and cultural programmes were over. To honour Swamishri the youths performed the traditional dance performed during the opening of Akshardham in New Delhi. Then Anandswarup Swami spoke on Swamishri’s works. Swamishri was then honoured with garlands by senior sadhus. The chief guests, Ralph O’Connor and Dr Kulin Pandya, were honoured and blessed on stage. Thereafter Anirdesh Swami and Atmatrupt Swami inspired all devotees to take one step forward in Satsang by making moral and spiritual pledges. Finally, Swamishri blessed the function, “Today, in the festive celebration the sadhus have guided you on the purpose of one’s human birth on earth. God has endowed us with a human body and graced us with all senses and intellect. So whatever we do for God would not be enough. We remain indebted to someone who has helped us. Indian culture teaches us that we are indebted to parents and society. Likewise we are indebted to God for giving us this human birth. May we do good works: have darshan of God with our eyes, listen to his glory with our ears, walk to the mandir with our legs. So we must put our body to good use. God has given us everything but if he hadn’t given us intellect then we would not have progressed. Because of intellect we studied and graduated and acquired many things in life. The reason for whatever we have attained is God, dharma and our shastras.” Finally youths performed a dance on the lyrics “Akshar Purushottam nã dankã…” Swamishri also waved the flag and crowned the centenary celebration assembly.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the waiting room. Here Mohanbhai, head of the Human Resources department and a board member of the Infosys company, had come for darshan. With him was Abhay Jain, a board member of IIM. They have been very impressed after seeing Akshardham. Speaking about the work of Infosys, he said, "We give midday meals to twelve lakh (1.2 million) children every day. We run a scheme called Akshaya Patra in 7,800 schools."
Swamishri said, "God's grace will be greatly upon you." He also said, "The one who gives never runs short."
Hearing of their feeling, Swamishri's face was filled with emotion. He was pleased and gave special blessings that their wish would be fulfilled.
When Pramukh Swami Maharaj comes to the mandir for darshan, members of the children's mandal here give various presentations in the mandir courtyard.

Today, when Swamishri sat in the mandir's hydraulic lift to go for darshan, the children acted out the incident of Bechar Kisa from the time of Shastriji Maharaj. In this dialogue there came a sweet jibe, in which the devotees, addressing Shastriji Maharaj laughingly, said, "Swami! You are never satisfied with acquiring land. You are a true Patidar, aren't you!"

Swamishri was listening carefully to this dialogue. The lift was going up, and on hearing that sentence Swamishri burst out laughing and said, "Acquiring land after land, we have come all the way to Delhi."
Today Swamishri was in the mood of Shastriji Maharaj.

Although the monsoon had set in, the rain in Gujarat had been delayed. Sitting here, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was troubled by worry for Gujarat and wherever the shadow of drought lay. That is why today, before his puja began, Swamishri said, "Call the sadhu who does the announcements."
Munivatsal Swami came there immediately. Giving him instructions, Swamishri said, "Have a dhun chanted for half an hour every day during the puja. First have that dhun chanted."

Swamishri could not remember the tune, so we sadhus sang our standard dhun in raag Bhimpalas. Then Swamishri said, "Yes, that one. Have that dhun chanted for half an hour, and in between keep singing just two lines of 'Manno morliyo rate taru naam' (The peacock of my mind chants your name). Also keep 'Vadli utarje Ghelane teer' (O cloud, come down on the banks of the Ghela). In Gujarat and the country there is no rain or it has been delayed, so from today have only the dhun chanted every day in the puja, so that it rains everywhere."
In this way Swamishri began the practice of the dhun, and commanded that the dhun be chanted in all the mandirs of Gujarat and in India and abroad.
After the puja, when Swamishri came out, clouds really had gathered. The sadhus said, "The clouds have gathered."
Swamishri said, "Keep faith. Do not think it is all done."

In the courtyard of his residence, Aksharprem Swami and his group were chanting the dhun with the pakhavaj. Swamishri too spontaneously joined in and said, "Do such a dhun every day. Keep faith in God. Shraddhavan labhate gnanam (The one who has faith attains knowledge)."
After many days, monsoon clouds had gathered here too. In this context the sadhus said, "You did the dhun, and the clouds have gathered here."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj immediately said, "Here it does rain, but there (in Gujarat) the poor people's crops are drying up. The poor farmers sow as soon as there is one rain, and then when the rain is delayed, the seeds get burnt. Some say, 'The early riser gains,' and some say, 'The late riser gains,' but gain comes only by God's wish."
Seeing Swamishri's concern, the sadhus said, "Since you did the dhun, it will certainly rain."
Swamishri said, "In just one day? It should be kept going. I pray that there is a good, steady rain."

This morning Dr Nikul had taken Pramukh Swami Maharaj's blood. He inserted the needle once, but did not succeed. This was the first time this had happened. On the second attempt he took it. In this connection Dr Nikul said, "Bapa! Please forgive me. I troubled you twice."

In a completely natural manner, as if nothing had happened, Swamishri said in Hindi, "I have no pain at all, no joy or sorrow. So many needles have been put into this body and are still being put in, and it has been cut open here (the stomach) and cut open here too (the chest). Do not worry."
With such strengthening words of Swamishri, Nikul forgot his regret. This is exactly Swamishri's special quality.
A sadhu said, "Nikul says that you have reduced your eating so much that the vein cannot be found now. So please eat a little more."
Swamishri said, "That is in God's hands."
Swamishri behaves as the atma, so in any situation the joy of being brahmarup does not lessen in the least.

ds.t: "In the work of dharma, act quickly"
w: Ahmed Patel, National General Secretary of the Congress, came for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. With him were his
son Faisal, Firoz Bilakhia of Vapi of 'Micro Inc', his secretary Mahajanji, his PA in Bharuch Yunusbhai, and Ghanshyambhai of Secunderabad.
Ahmedbhai said, "I thought that you would be leaving in two days. If I had known that you were staying another ten or fifteen days, I would have come at leisure, taking more time."
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "We may well be here, but if you suddenly went out of town, it would be missed, wouldn't it! So in the work of dharma, act quickly, do it soon."
How wonderful Swamishri's quickness of mind and courtesy are, even at this age!

Kamath Saheb, Chairman of Punjab National Bank, came for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. With him came Executive Directors Mohan and Shri Nagesh, General Manager Khanna, and Branch Managers Singh and Gupta.

Swamishri said to the Chairman, "We have to take out time for the world, we do take out time for worldly dealings. It is good to take out time for God. Through it there is peace and one gets success."

Shri Kamath said, "I came here with my family. I stayed here for four hours. I liked it so much, the pressure I had was released. For three or four hours there was no pressure. Coming here, I forgot the world."

Another of his officers said, "I too came here. Seeing this, my daughter said to me, 'Why do people call other places in India a Wonder of the World? This mandir should be called a Wonder of the World.'"

Hearing of their feelings, Swamishri's face became full of emotion. He was pleased and gave special blessings that their wish be fulfilled.

ds.t: Without katha, what is there to do
w: Today, because of the tenth anniversary celebration of the Atlanta mandir, the programme was packed. To save Mahant Swami Maharaj's time, no blessings had been scheduled, but Swamishri himself expressed a wish to speak. And he spoke powerfully for 25 minutes without a break. So as he was leaving the assembly, Anupamdas Swami folded his hands and said to Swamishri, "Swami! We had not scheduled a talk so as to save your time."
Swamishri said, "So that is why you had not scheduled katha? Without katha, what is there to do?"
There was a feeling in Swamishri's words that brought to mind these words of Pramukh Swami Maharaj: "This little soul is made of katha and spiritual talks..."
When Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his meal, on the occasion of today's tenth anniversary celebration, Gnanpriyadas Swami fed Swamishri puranpoli.

Swamishri himself also asked Viveknidhidas Swami to come and serve. He came forward, delighted. Serving Swamishri, he said, "I had wished that I might get to serve Swamishri, and you called me yourself and fulfilled my wish."
Swamishri keeps fulfilling hundreds and thousands of such wishes, small and large. Some come to light and are noted, and some remain only within that person's mind and heart.

ds.t: An angel come down to earth
w: Today, during Mahant Swami Maharaj's evening meal, Shobhitswarupdas Swami told of an incident:

"Hareshbhai Lakhani, the chief disciple here of Sri Sri Ravi Shankarji, had come for Swamishri's darshan. He lives in Tampa. In the personal meetings he had darshan for barely ten seconds. He said, 'In just this ten seconds of darshan, a tingling spread through my whole body. I experienced complete peace. And I felt as if, in a fraction of a second, all my chakras had been activated.'"
Gunsagardas Swami told of another:

"Kapil Chothani works at SOKI, a mobile device management company. He was watching live the welcome you received in London on 15 June. He told me of the experience he had from this darshan. Let us hear it in his own words. He said:

'Seeing Swamishri entering the welcome assembly holding Harikrishna Maharaj in his hands, tears welled up in my eyes. The hairs on my body stood on end. To tell the truth, the process of transferring my conviction from Pramukh Swami Maharaj to Mahant Swami Maharaj had been hard for me, but in this darshan I felt the very same experience, the very same excitement, as when Pramukh Swami Maharaj came here to America in 2014!

And moreover, while I was watching this live darshan, the director of my company came and stood beside me to watch it. Seeing him, four or five others also gathered. The director had darshan on the screen for the very first time and immediately exclaimed, "Your guru is divine. The divinity in his eyes and spark on his face are priceless. Are you sure he is not the angel come down on this earth?"
Hearing this, my excitement grew even more, the hairs on my body stood on end even more, and a stream of tears began to flow from my eyes.'"
In the evening, the attendant sadhu said to Mahant Swami Maharaj, "Swami! The tenth anniversary programme is at 8 o'clock. It is now 7.30 and it has started raining."
Swamishri too was a little startled and exclaimed, "What!"

He immediately asked the sadhus sitting in front of him to do a dhun, and he himself closed his eyes and began chanting. He came to his room and the chesta began, and on this side, looking out of the window, the sun had come out again. This time there was a real game of rain and sunshine. It would rain, Swamishri would do dhun, and the sun would come out; then rain again, then sun again. But in the end, Indra, the god of rain, obeyed Swamishri's command. The rain stopped completely.
This is the Gunatit way. Did not Gunatitanand Swami protect Lalabhai of Upleta in just this way!

In Vachanamrut Gadhada I 27, Shriji Maharaj has said, "To be forbearing despite being powerful is something no one can do. One who is forbearing in this way should be known to be extremely great." Though Swamishri is powerful, he has a dhun done; if this is not forbearance, what is?
